USER: Hi, I need to understand my new insurance plan from my employer.
ASSISTANT: Good morning! I'm Sandra from BlueCross BlueShield Member Services. I'll help you understand your coverage. What's your member ID?
USER: It's BCS8829447.
ASSISTANT: Thank you, Mr... let me pull this up... Mr. Robert Thompson?
USER: Yes, that's me.
ASSISTANT: I see you have our PPO Select plan through Morrison Industries. Is this your first time with BlueCross?
USER: No, but my previous employer had a different BlueCross plan.
ASSISTANT: Good, so you're familiar with our network. This PPO Select plan has some great benefits. Your deductible is $1,500 individual, $3,000 family.
USER: Is that in-network?
ASSISTANT: Yes, in-network. Out-of-network is $3,000 individual, $6,000 family.
USER: What about the out-of-pocket maximum?
ASSISTANT: In-network maximum is $4,000 individual, $8,000 family. That includes your deductible.
USER: So once I pay $4,000, everything else is covered?
ASSISTANT: For in-network covered services, yes, we pay 100% after that.
USER: What about preventive care?
ASSISTANT: Preventive care is 100% covered, no deductible. Annual physicals, screenings, vaccinations.
USER: Good. What about specialist visits?
ASSISTANT: After deductible, you pay 20% coinsurance for specialists in-network.
USER: Do I need referrals?
ASSISTANT: No, with PPO you can see specialists directly.
USER: What about emergency room visits?
ASSISTANT: $350 copay plus 20% after deductible.
USER: That seems high.
ASSISTANT: ER is expensive. Urgent care is only $75 copay for non-emergency issues.
USER: Makes sense. What about prescriptions?
ASSISTANT: Generic drugs are $10, preferred brand $35, non-preferred brand $70, specialty drugs 30% up to $250.
USER: My wife takes Synthroid for thyroid. Is that covered?
ASSISTANT: Synthroid is a preferred brand, so $35 per month.
USER: What about surgery coverage?
ASSISTANT: Inpatient surgery is 20% after deductible. Outpatient surgery is also 20% after deductible.
USER: So if I needed knee surgery?
ASSISTANT: Depends if it's inpatient or outpatient. Most knee surgeries are outpatient now. You'd pay your deductible first, then 20%.
USER: Actually, I've been having knee problems. My doctor mentioned I might need arthroscopy.
ASSISTANT: Arthroscopy is typically outpatient. Do you know the estimated cost?
USER: No idea.
ASSISTANT: Usually runs $15,000-25,000 total. With your plan, after $1,500 deductible, you'd pay 20% of the remainder.
USER: So potentially $3,000-4,000 out of pocket?
ASSISTANT: With the $4,000 out-of-pocket max, you'd never pay more than that in a year.
USER: That's still a lot.
ASSISTANT: You might want to check if your employer offers an FSA or HSA to save pre-tax.
USER: What's the difference?
ASSISTANT: FSA is use-it-or-lose-it yearly. HSA rolls over but you need a high-deductible health plan.
USER: This isn't high-deductible?
ASSISTANT: No, $1,500 is considered standard. High-deductible starts at $1,600 for 2024.
USER: So I could do FSA?
ASSISTANT: Yes, check with your HR about FSA enrollment.
USER: Back to coverage - what about physical therapy?
ASSISTANT: PT is covered, 30 visits per year. You pay 20% after deductible.
USER: That might be relevant if I need knee surgery.
ASSISTANT: Exactly. Most knee procedures need 10-20 PT sessions.
USER: Is there prior authorization needed?
ASSISTANT: For surgery, yes. Your doctor submits that. PT doesn't need prior auth for the first 10 visits.
USER: What about MRIs?
ASSISTANT: MRIs need prior authorization and you pay 20% after deductible.
USER: My doctor already ordered an MRI for my knee.
ASSISTANT: Make sure they get prior auth first. Otherwise, you might pay full price.
USER: How do I check that?
ASSISTANT: Call the imaging center and confirm they've received authorization. I can also check if you have the facility name.
USER: It's Premier Imaging on Riverside Drive.
ASSISTANT: Let me check... I don't see a prior auth yet. When is your MRI scheduled?
USER: Next month, February 20th.
ASSISTANT: Have your doctor submit the prior auth request soon. It takes 5-7 business days.
USER: I'll call them tomorrow. What else should I know?
ASSISTANT: Keep all receipts for tax purposes. Medical expenses over 7.5% of income are deductible.
USER: Good tip. Is there anything this plan doesn't cover?
ASSISTANT: Cosmetic procedures, weight loss surgery unless medically necessary, experimental treatments.
USER: What about mental health?
ASSISTANT: Mental health is covered same as medical - 20% after deductible for therapy.
USER: And dental?
ASSISTANT: Dental is separate. Do you have dental through your employer too?
USER: Yes, but I haven't looked at it yet.
ASSISTANT: Check that separately. Medical doesn't cover dental except for accident-related injuries.
USER: Got it. What about vision?
ASSISTANT: Vision is also separate. Medical covers eye injuries and diseases, not routine exams or glasses.
USER: My employer offers vision too. I should review that.
ASSISTANT: Yes, especially if you wear glasses or contacts. Those benefits are usually worth it.
USER: Is there a nurse hotline or something if I have questions?
ASSISTANT: Yes, 24/7 nurse line at 800-555-NURSE. Great for after-hours medical questions.
USER: That's helpful. And you mentioned an app?
ASSISTANT: Yes, the BlueCross app. You can check claims, find providers, even video chat with doctors.
USER: Video visits are covered?
ASSISTANT: Yes, $20 copay for video visits with our partner Teladoc. Great for minor issues.
USER: Much cheaper than urgent care.
ASSISTANT: Exactly. Use it for colds, rashes, minor infections. They can even prescribe medications.
USER: This is all really helpful. Thanks Sandra!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome Mr. Thompson. Don't forget to ask HR about that FSA option. And good luck with your knee!

USER: Hi, I need to schedule knee surgery with Dr. Martinez.
ASSISTANT: Good afternoon! This is Lisa from Advanced Orthopedic Center. You're scheduling surgery with Dr. Martinez?
USER: Yes, I saw him last week and he said I need arthroscopic surgery for my torn meniscus.
ASSISTANT: Let me pull up your chart. Your name?
USER: Robert Thompson.
ASSISTANT: Date of birth?
USER: May 15, 1978.
ASSISTANT: I see your appointment from November 13th. Dr. Martinez recommended arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
USER: That's right. He said it's pretty routine.
ASSISTANT: It is, Dr. Martinez does several each week. When would you like to schedule?
USER: As soon as possible. My knee is really bothering me.
ASSISTANT: I have an opening December 5th at our surgery center.
USER: That works. What time?
ASSISTANT: 7:30 AM arrival, surgery at 8:30 AM. You'll be done by 10 AM.
USER: Good, I can take the whole day off work.
ASSISTANT: You'll want someone to drive you home after anesthesia.
USER: My wife can do that.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Now, which surgery center location - Riverside or Northside?
USER: Which is closer to downtown?
ASSISTANT: Riverside is closer, about 10 minutes from downtown.
USER: Let's do Riverside then.
ASSISTANT: Riverside Surgery Center, December 5th, 7:30 AM arrival. What insurance do you have?
USER: BlueCross BlueShield PPO.
ASSISTANT: Good, we're in-network. Has Dr. Martinez's office started the prior authorization?
USER: He said they would handle it.
ASSISTANT: Let me check... I don't see it yet. We need authorization before surgery.
USER: How long does that take?
ASSISTANT: Usually 5-7 business days. I'll have our insurance coordinator expedite it.
USER: Please do. I don't want any delays.
ASSISTANT: Of course. Now, the facility fee for the surgery center is $18,500.
USER: Eighteen thousand?! For outpatient surgery?
ASSISTANT: That includes the OR, equipment, nursing staff, and recovery room.
USER: What about the surgeon's fee?
ASSISTANT: Dr. Martinez's fee is separate, approximately $4,800.
USER: So over $23,000 total?
ASSISTANT: Plus anesthesia, which is usually $1,500-2,000.
USER: This is getting expensive. What will I actually pay?
ASSISTANT: That depends on your insurance benefits. Do you know your deductible?
USER: I think it's $1,500.
ASSISTANT: And your coinsurance after deductible?
USER: Twenty percent I believe.
ASSISTANT: So roughly $1,500 deductible plus 20% of the remaining $23,500, which is about $4,700.
USER: Wait, that math doesn't seem right.
ASSISTANT: Let me recalculate. Total about $25,000 with anesthesia. Minus $1,500 deductible leaves $23,500. Twenty percent of that is $4,700. Plus the $1,500 deductible equals $6,200.
USER: Six thousand dollars?!
ASSISTANT: Do you have an out-of-pocket maximum?
USER: I think it's $4,000.
ASSISTANT: Then you'd pay at most $4,000 for the year. Have you had any other medical expenses this year?
USER: Just my MRI and some doctor visits.
ASSISTANT: Those count toward your deductible and maximum. Do you know how much you've paid so far?
USER: Maybe $800 total?
ASSISTANT: So you'd likely pay another $3,200 to hit your maximum.
USER: That's still a lot. Can I make payments?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we offer payment plans. We require 20% down, then 12 months interest-free.
USER: So $800 down if I owe $4,000?
ASSISTANT: If you owe $3,200 after your previous payments, it would be $640 down.
USER: Then what monthly?
ASSISTANT: The remaining $2,560 over 12 months is about $213 per month.
USER: That's manageable. What about the anesthesia bill?
ASSISTANT: Anesthesia bills separately. They're with Riverside Anesthesia Group.
USER: Are they in-network?
ASSISTANT: I need to verify that. Sometimes anesthesiologists are out-of-network even at in-network facilities.
USER: That doesn't seem fair.
ASSISTANT: I agree. Let me check... Good news, Riverside Anesthesia Group is in-network with BlueCross.
USER: Relief! What do I need to do before surgery?
ASSISTANT: Pre-op testing - blood work, EKG if you're over 40.
USER: I'm 46, so I'll need the EKG.
ASSISTANT: Yes. You can do pre-op testing here November 28th at 2 PM.
USER: That works. No eating before surgery, right?
ASSISTANT: Nothing after midnight the night before. Clear liquids until 4 AM.
USER: What about my medications?
ASSISTANT: What do you take regularly?
USER: Just blood pressure medication - lisinopril.
ASSISTANT: Take that with a small sip of water the morning of surgery.
USER: How long is recovery?
ASSISTANT: You'll use crutches for a few days, then physical therapy starts week two.
USER: How many PT sessions?
ASSISTANT: Typically 12-16 sessions over 6-8 weeks.
USER: Is PT covered by insurance?
ASSISTANT: You'll want to verify your PT benefits. Most plans have visit limits.
USER: I think mine covers 30 visits per year.
ASSISTANT: That should be plenty. We'll give you a PT prescription after surgery.
USER: Do you recommend any specific PT places?
ASSISTANT: We work closely with Riverside Rehab and Downtown Physical Therapy. Both are excellent.
USER: Are they in-network?
ASSISTANT: You'll need to check with your insurance, but they take most major plans.
USER: When can I return to work?
ASSISTANT: Desk job?
USER: Yes, I'm in IT.
ASSISTANT: You could work from home after 3-4 days, return to office after a week.
USER: That's not too bad. When can I drive?
ASSISTANT: Once you're off narcotic pain meds, usually 3-5 days.
USER: And exercise? I usually run.
ASSISTANT: No running for 6-8 weeks. Start with walking, then bike, then elliptical.
USER: That's a long time.
ASSISTANT: Better to heal properly than re-injure it. Dr. Martinez will give you a specific timeline.
USER: Makes sense. So I'm all scheduled?
ASSISTANT: Yes! December 5th surgery, November 28th pre-op. We'll call you December 4th with final instructions.
USER: Perfect. Thanks for all the information!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome Mr. Thompson. See you November 28th for pre-op testing!

USER: Hi, I'm having surgery next month and want to understand your billing.
ASSISTANT: Good afternoon, this is Mark from Riverside Anesthesia billing. I can help explain our charges. What type of surgery?
USER: Knee arthroscopy on December 5th at Riverside Surgery Center.
ASSISTANT: Okay, arthroscopy typically takes 30-45 minutes of anesthesia time.
USER: How do you calculate the charges?
ASSISTANT: We bill by time units. Base units for knee arthroscopy plus time units.
USER: What does that mean in dollars?
ASSISTANT: For a 45-minute procedure, typically $1,800-2,200 total charges.
USER: Someone told me you might not be in my insurance network?
ASSISTANT: What insurance do you have?
USER: BlueCross BlueShield PPO.
ASSISTANT: Good news - we're in-network with BlueCross PPO.
USER: Oh thank goodness! Someone scared me about surprise bills.
ASSISTANT: That happens with out-of-network anesthesiologists. We've been with BlueCross for years.
USER: So same benefits as my surgery - deductible and coinsurance?
ASSISTANT: Exactly. Your regular in-network benefits apply.
USER: The surgery center said I'd hit my out-of-pocket max.
ASSISTANT: Then our services might be fully covered if you've already hit the max.
USER: How does that work?
ASSISTANT: Once you've paid your maximum, insurance pays 100% of covered services.
USER: But I haven't had the surgery yet.
ASSISTANT: Right, but if the facility and surgeon fees hit your max, anesthesia would be covered.
USER: The facility is charging $18,500 and surgeon $4,800.
ASSISTANT: With a $4,000 out-of-pocket max, you'd hit it with just those charges.
USER: So I might not owe you anything?
ASSISTANT: Potentially, yes. We bill in order received, so timing matters.
USER: What do you mean?
ASSISTANT: If the facility bills first and uses up your maximum, we're covered. If we bill first, you'd owe part of ours.
USER: That seems arbitrary.
ASSISTANT: It can be. Most facilities bill quickly though, so they usually process first.
USER: Should I do anything special?
ASSISTANT: Make sure all providers have your correct insurance info.
USER: I gave it to the surgery center.
ASSISTANT: We'll get it from them, but verify day of surgery too.
USER: Will do. Do you require payment upfront?
ASSISTANT: No, we bill insurance first, then send you any balance.
USER: How long does that take?
ASSISTANT: Usually 30-45 days after surgery for insurance to process.
USER: And if I owe something?
ASSISTANT: We offer payment plans if the balance is over $500.
USER: Good to know. Oh, I take blood pressure medication. Is that an issue?
ASSISTANT: What medication specifically?
USER: Lisinopril.
ASSISTANT: That's fine. Take it the morning of surgery with minimal water.
USER: The surgery center said the same thing.
ASSISTANT: Good, consistency is important. Any other medications?
USER: No, just vitamins.
ASSISTANT: Stop vitamins a week before surgery. Some can affect bleeding.
USER: Oh, I didn't know that!
ASSISTANT: Especially vitamin E, fish oil, and herbal supplements.
USER: I take fish oil for cholesterol.
ASSISTANT: Definitely stop that now, two weeks before surgery is ideal.
USER: Two weeks? Surgery is December 5th, that's less than two weeks away!
ASSISTANT: Stop it immediately then. The sooner the better.
USER: Will do today. Why does it matter?
ASSISTANT: Fish oil can thin your blood and increase bleeding risk during surgery.
USER: That sounds serious.
ASSISTANT: It's a precaution. Stopping now gives your body time to normalize.
USER: What about aspirin?
ASSISTANT: Do you take aspirin regularly?
USER: No, just occasionally for headaches.
ASSISTANT: Avoid it before surgery. Use Tylenol instead if needed.
USER: Good to know. Anything else I should know?
ASSISTANT: Don't wear nail polish - we monitor oxygen through your fingernail.
USER: I'm a guy, so no problem there!
ASSISTANT: Also, arrange your ride home. You can't drive for 24 hours after anesthesia.
USER: My wife is taking the day off.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Oh, one more thing - have you had anesthesia before?
USER: Yes, for my wisdom teeth about 10 years ago.
ASSISTANT: Any problems with it?
USER: I was really nauseous afterward.
ASSISTANT: Important to know. I'll note that in your chart.
USER: Can you prevent that?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we can give anti-nausea medication preventively.
USER: That would be great. I don't want to feel sick.
ASSISTANT: The anesthesiologist will discuss options with you morning of surgery.
USER: Do I meet them beforehand?
ASSISTANT: Yes, they'll talk to you in pre-op before taking you to surgery.
USER: Good, I like to know who's putting me under.
ASSISTANT: Absolutely. They'll review your history and answer any questions.
USER: Perfect. Thanks for all the information, Mark!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome! Good luck with your surgery December 5th. Remember to stop that fish oil today!
